scope: Corollary 6.5 (Initial-form Milnor-fibre counterexamples) of the manuscript “Ambiently homeomorphic isolated hypersurfaces of multiplicities two and three” (preprints/Ambiently-homeomorphic-isolated-hypersurfaces-of-multiplicities-two-and-three-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 059 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ce7e450c32aa20ca), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 26. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In the single ambient dimension N + 1, put e fj(z, t) = fj(z) + t2 , j = 1, 2. The germs e f1, e f2 : (CN+1, 0) → (C, 0) are topologically right equivalent and have isolated critical points at the origin, but H0 ( e f1)−1 ∗ (1); Z  ∼ = Z, H0 ( e f2)−1 ∗ (1); Z  ∼ = Z2 . Thus integral homology of the initial-form Milnor fibre is not invariant under topological right equivalence, already in degree zero. In particular, the initial-form Milnor-fibre homotopy conjecture of Budur, Fernández de Bobadilla, Lê, and Nguyen [3, Conjecture 1.7 in arXiv v3] fails.
